A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Feature-Projective DP work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support matching content across the revised organization.

before.justification: v3 reports original MPII and HumanART experiments comparing private training methods, privacy budgets, clipping thresholds, and initialization strategies, including appendix tables and qualitative predictions.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and qualitative results, and additionally reports non-private HumanART reference scores.

M1.justification: The architecture, loss decomposition, and projection procedure remain intact. However, Equations 4 and 9 and Algorithm 1 change the written noise normalization from (sum gradients)/B + noise to (sum gradients + noise)/B. This changes the specified update; the PDFs do not establish an implementation change or rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions use COCO pretraining and evaluate on MPII and HumanART. HumanART's artistic-domain coverage already appears in v3's main text and appendix; its expanded prominence in v4 does not introduce a new dataset or task.

E2.justification: v4 adds non-private frozen-backbone and full-fine-tuning references to the HumanART comparison in Section 4.3, with a non-private reference also plotted in Figure 3. The evaluated DP-SGD, projection, Feature DP, and combined private-method comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 presents HumanART results under PCKh/per-joint descriptions and joint-labelled columns. v4 specifies COCO-style AP/AR evaluation and changes those column headings accordingly. This revises the reported metrics, although the numerical entries are identical and no rerun is established. Training budgets, privacy settings, and initialization strategies are otherwise retained.

E4.justification: The component comparisons, clipping/privacy sweeps, training-strategy comparisons, and qualitative cases are retained. The new HumanART visualization largely redisplays existing appendix results; expanded explanations do not establish new ablation or robustness experiments.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Reported means summarize task performance rather than newly introduced statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: All matched detailed table scores remain unchanged. v4 newly reports HumanART non-private scores of 63.3 AP for frozen-backbone fine-tuning and 69.5 AP for full fine-tuning, and asserts 73% privacy-gap recovery. Its conclusion changes MPII performance from 82.61% to 82.62%, matching the retained table, although the abstract still says 82.61%.

T1.justification: v3 has DP/FDP definitions and algorithm equations but no convergence analysis. v4 adds Section 3.4.3 and Appendix A.1, introducing smoothness, bounded-gradient, and subspace assumptions and an expected-gradient-norm bound separating privacy and reconstruction errors. It also compares dimensionality and sensitivity dependence across the component methods. The bound is stated as a corollary rather than fully derived.

C1.justification: v4 expands the contribution from an empirically effective combination into a claimed theoretical multiplicative improvement in signal-to-noise ratio and convergence speed. Its abstract explicitly claims k/p noise-variance reduction and 73% privacy-gap recovery. The underlying first-DP-HPE positioning and combined-method contribution remain.

C2.justification: v4 adds parameter-count reasoning for choosing TinyViT and explains HumanART's reversal between frozen and full fine-tuning under DP through noise and clipping. Its new categorical statement that C=1.0 yields negligible HumanART accuracy is too broad: retained Table 10 reports up to 35.4 AP under that setting.

D1.justification: v4 adds a project-page URL in the abstract. Existing implementation disclosures remain: 25 epochs, 256×192 inputs, RDP accounting, 100 public projection samples, projection dimension 50, and the specified Gaussian blur. No additional hardware, optimizer, or experimental seed details appear.

R1.justification: v4 supplements related work with privacy-onion, instance-encoding/adversarial, mixed-DP, recent pose-estimation, and reconstruction literature. Additional DP theory and model-size references support the new analysis and interpretation. These broaden the discussion without replacing the original research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and related-work discussion are substantially rewritten. v4 introduces numbered section hierarchies, separates feature privacy from combined-method training, creates a main-text HumanART discussion, and organizes the expanded appendix into labelled sections.

P2.justification: v4 redraws MPII Figure 2 from nine panels to six, retaining omitted random-initialization results in tables; adds HumanART Figure 3 and notation Table 2; corrects HumanART table headings; and substantially rearranges and resizes displays. The qualitative images are retained. The new HumanART figure incorrectly labels its AP axes as PCKh@0.5.

improvement.justification: Correcting HumanART's misleading table headings, adding non-private reference scores, and explicitly stating the combined method's theoretical assumptions improve interpretability. The gain is limited: the detailed experimental evidence is unchanged, the convergence bound lacks a full derivation, and v4 introduces inconsistencies, notably Figure 3's metric labels and the C=1.0 failure claim contradicted by Table 10. These prevent a substantial overall improvement.
